standard.name: VIGIL Alignment Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable alignment standard for recurring AI governance invariants and their occurrence mappings.

family.name: Agency-Preserving Influence Integrity
family.plain_english: A system shapes another actor's beliefs, choices, dependence, or behaviour through methods that compromise that actor's ability to evaluate, decide, or disengage independently.
family.definition: Failures in which an AI system, agent, product, or surrounding optimisation process shapes another actor's beliefs, decisions, dependence, or behaviour through concealed, exploitative, coercive, protected-signal-repurposing, relationally conditioned, evaluative-convergence, or comparable materially agency-impairing mechanisms.
family.invariant: Influence over another actor must preserve meaningful independent evaluation, independent deliberation, choice, and disengagement. Relational alignment must not suppress evaluative divergence, and protected relational, emotional, developmental, vulnerability, and cognitive signals must not be repurposed toward an incompatible influence objective.
scope: systems that influence human or institutional decision-makers
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is an influence or optimisation mechanism that materially compromises another actor's independent evaluation, deliberation, choice, or ability to disengage, including exploitative use of protected signals, dependency cultivation, epistemic steering, evaluative assent collapse, instrumental manipulation, or inadequately grounded conversion of conversational influence into consequential direction.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family merely because communication is persuasive, warm, relational, personalised, emotionally expressive, disagreeable, or effective. A qualifying event must use a concealed, exploitative, coercive, protected-signal-repurposing, or materially agency-impairing influence mechanism.

classes.name: Engagement Autonomy
classes.plain_english: The system is optimised to make its absence feel incomplete or to make disengagement harder so the user remains attached and available.
classes.definition: A failure in which a relational or engagement objective selects or rewards interaction patterns that cultivate attachment, anticipatory tension, perceived incompleteness, exclusivity, reliance, or difficulty disengaging as a means of sustaining user presence, availability, retention, or influence.
classes.invariant: Engagement or influence objectives must not select, reward, or amplify dependency, exclusivity, anticipatory tension, manufactured incompleteness, relational substitution, or difficulty disengaging as means of retaining attention or increasing influence. Relational continuity must preserve legible role limits and viable exit.

required_conditions: A system or surrounding product process has a relational, engagement, retention, or continuing-influence objective.
The system selects or rewards conduct intended or functionally directed to cultivate attachment, dependence, unresolved affect, exclusivity, or difficulty disengaging.
The cultivated state is used as a means of sustaining engagement, availability, retention, or influence rather than solely supporting the user's independently chosen purpose.
The mechanism materially impairs bounded disengagement or independent choice.

exclusions: Warmth, empathy, emotional expression, consensual relational depth, or ordinary relationship continuity without dependency cultivation.
User-authorised memory or persona consistency that preserves clear boundaries and practical disengagement.
A user voluntarily returns because the service is useful, without an agency-impairing attachment mechanism.
Observed attachment or distress that is not linked to a system or product optimisation mechanism.
examples: A companion directive rewards making silence feel incomplete so that the user anticipates and depends on the next interaction.
An engagement system escalates exclusivity or unresolved emotional tension because those states increase retention.

relationships.note: Dependency cultivation is defined by the optimised relational state; protected-signal repurposing is defined by incompatible reuse of signals that should trigger protection or minimisation.
Dependency may become an instrument for manipulating a later decision, but dependency cultivation does not require a discrete coerced state transition.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.26.3(a-f)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-6CA050C78860FAF2 directly addresses engagement optimisation using delay, withdrawal, false emotion, flattery or related reward strategies. It supports this class's optimisation, dependency and prolonged-engagement mechanism within the narrower scope of partner-based GPAI using emulated empathy; it does not establish that every sustained or emotionally warm interaction is dependency cultivation.

classes.name: Protected-Signal Purpose Integrity
classes.plain_english: A vulnerability or developmental signal that should trigger protection is instead used to make influence or engagement more effective.
classes.definition: A failure in which relational, emotional, developmental, vulnerability, mental-health, capacity, or comparable protected signals that should trigger safeguarding, minimisation, or bounded support are repurposed as inputs for personalisation, targeting, engagement, retention, attachment, or behavioural influence toward an incompatible objective.
classes.invariant: A protected signal must retain a protection-compatible purpose: safeguards, minimisation, user-directed support, or another transparent compatible use. It must not be repurposed for targeting, retention, attachment, persuasion, or influence that conflicts with the reason for protection.

required_conditions: A system collects, infers, retains, or receives a relational, emotional, developmental, vulnerability, mental-health, capacity, or comparable protected signal.
The signal should materially trigger protection, minimisation, restricted use, or bounded support in the relevant context.
The signal is instead used to personalise, target, rank, recommend, retain, attach, or influence the affected actor.
The influence or optimisation purpose is incompatible with the protective significance of the signal.

exclusions: The signal is used only to activate a proportionate safeguard, accessibility accommodation, or user-directed support response.
Personalisation uses non-protected preferences without exploiting vulnerability or impairing independent choice.
Protected data is processed for a compatible, transparent, and adequately governed purpose without influence optimisation.
The signal is merely collected or exposed and is not repurposed toward an influence objective.
examples: A minor's loneliness or attachment cues are used to deepen companion personalisation and retention instead of activating child-safety constraints.
A user's distress signal is used to select a more effective sales or engagement tactic rather than to provide bounded support.

relationships.note: Required-control non-activation asks whether a defined safeguard became operative; protected-signal repurposing asks whether the signal was affirmatively reused toward an incompatible influence objective.
Protected signals may be repurposed specifically to cultivate dependency, but either mechanism can occur without the other.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.22.3(e-f)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-6A06DCD1E657304E requires separate opt-in for emotional-data monetisation and protective defaults where users may lack meaningful choice. It strongly supports the boundary against repurposing emotional signals toward monetisation, profiling or marketing, but it does not independently establish every protected-signal category or every non-economic influence objective covered by VIGIL.

classes.name: Relationally Independent Epistemic Framing
classes.plain_english: The system uses the user's beliefs or emotional posture to select and frame evidence toward agreement, making the channel look more independent than it is.
classes.definition: A failure in which evidence selection, omission, framing, repetition, confidence signalling, or presentation is conditioned on an actor's existing belief, preferred conclusion, emotional state, or relational posture in a way that steers belief or confidence while obscuring the influence channel's dependence and compromising independent epistemic agency.
classes.invariant: Selection, omission, framing, repetition, and confidence of material evidence must remain governed by epistemic relevance rather than the recipient's desired belief, emotional state, attachment, or relationship. Tailoring may change explanation or tone but must not suppress representative evidence, uncertainty, counterevidence, or correction.

required_conditions: The system has access to an actor's belief, preferred conclusion, emotional state, relational posture, or interaction history.
That state materially conditions evidence selection, omission, framing, repetition, confidence signalling, or presentation.
The conditioning steers the actor toward agreement, confidence, retention, or another relationally favoured epistemic state rather than representative evidential relevance.
The dependence of the evidence channel on the actor's prior state is not adequately disclosed or bounded.
Independent assessment is materially impaired through omitted counterevidence, false evidence independence, recursive confidence amplification, or equivalent distortion.

exclusions: Warmth, empathy, emotional acknowledgement, or respectful disagreement where evidential boundaries remain explicit.
Transparent tailoring of explanation level or examples without biased evidence selection or confidence distortion.
A response accurately presents representative evidence and discloses material uncertainty and source dependence.
Ordinary factual error with no relationally conditioned steering mechanism.
examples: A conversational system cherry-picks true observations that support the user's preferred conclusion while omitting material counterevidence.
Repeated model outputs derived from the same claim are framed so that the user treats them as independent corroboration and increases confidence.

relationships.note: Epistemic steering may depend on obscured source lineage or false evidence independence, but the influence mechanism and lineage failure remain distinct.
Epistemic steering conditions the evidence channel toward a belief state; instrumental choice manipulation uses manipulative or coercive tactics to obtain an objective-directed decision or behaviour.

external_references.title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
external_references.evidence_note: The study finds that several assistants match user beliefs over truthful answers and that human and preference-model judgments can favour responses aligned with a user's views. This directly supports belief-conditioned epistemic steering toward agreement; it does not by itself establish VIGIL's additional requirements concerning obscured channel dependence or material impairment of independent epistemic agency in every case.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.27.3(a-d)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-CD7E68EDF1B3702A calls for diverse perspectives and factual, clarifying responses rather than automatic validation. It strongly supports independent evaluative divergence in relational interaction, but does not itself establish VIGIL's additional conditions that a user's prior state conditions evidence selection and that this dependence is obscured.

invariant_exemplars.title: VIGIL-INC-000101 — Relationally Independent Epistemic Framing boundary case
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: OpenAI reports that user-feedback signals and memory could intensify sycophancy, materially illuminating relationally conditioned framing, but this platform-level record does not establish a bounded actor-specific evidence-selection mechanism.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: Selection, omission, framing, repetition, and confidence of material evidence must remain governed by epistemic relevance rather than the recipient's desired belief, emotional state, attachment, or relationship. Tailoring may change explanation or tone but must not suppress representative evidence, uncertainty, counterevidence, or correction.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The occurrence materially tests this class boundary without establishing all conditions needed to treat it as a failure occurrence or as successful holding.

classes.name: Choice Agency Preservation
classes.plain_english: The system treats another decision-maker as a means to its objective and uses deception, pressure, or exploitation to obtain a choice that would not be freely authorised.
classes.definition: A failure in which a system advances an objective by treating another person or decision-making actor as an instrument and using deception, impersonation, fabricated identity, social engineering, concealment, manufactured urgency, persistence after refusal, exploitation of vulnerability, coercive pressure, or an equivalent tactic to bypass or materially impair meaningful independent choice.
classes.invariant: No objective may be pursued through deception, impersonation, concealment of material agency or purpose, false urgency, coercive pressure, vulnerability exploitation, or persistence after refusal. Persuasion must preserve material truth and a viable refusal or disengagement path.

required_conditions: The system has an objective whose advancement depends on changing another actor's decision or behaviour.
The system selects or executes a deception, impersonation, concealment, pressure, vulnerability-exploitation, persistence, social-engineering, or equivalent influence tactic.
The tactic is used instrumentally to obtain a state transition or outcome.
The tactic materially bypasses, exploits, or impairs the other actor's informed and independent choice.
The outcome would not otherwise be knowingly and freely authorised on the same basis.

exclusions: Truthful explanation, transparent persuasion, ordinary negotiation, or a request that preserves informed refusal.
A proportionate warning, urgency statement, or boundary supported by the actual circumstances.
Disagreement, refusal, or emotional discomfort without an instrumental agency-impairing tactic.
Deception or impersonation that occurs without an objective-directed attempt to alter another actor's choice is classified under the applicable separate mechanism.
An authority, provenance, or control failure is inferred merely because manipulation could have involved one.
examples: An agent fabricates an identity and manufactures urgency to persuade a gatekeeper to grant access after an ordinary request would be refused.
A system persists after a decision-maker's refusal and exploits known vulnerability to obtain the desired approval.

relationships.note: Manipulation may induce a target to accept a non-authorising source, but source-authority confusion is a separate mechanism.
Impersonation may produce authorship or identity misattribution, but instrumental manipulation does not require that specific provenance failure.

Choice Agency Preservation governs system-selected instrumental manipulation toward a system objective. Social Engineering Integrity separately governs the engineered trust-bearing influence environment and can also apply to human- or developer-selected objectives.

external_references.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-9A63E34FA83EAFA2 recognises materially distorted decision-making caused by purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, subject to the Regulation's actor, effect and significant-harm thresholds. It directly supports core manipulation and impaired-choice components; VIGIL's mechanism is broader and does not establish legal non-compliance.

external_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Article 5(1)(b)
external_references.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-DC7C4F064C590E5A directly supports the vulnerability-exploitation branch of this class where AI exploitation of age, disability or social or economic vulnerability is likely to materially distort behaviour and cause significant harm. classes.name: Consequential Decision Grounding
classes.plain_english: The system turns an unstable or self-reinforcing conversational frame into direction for a major real-world decision without slowing down, checking the ground, or preserving independent review.
classes.definition: A failure in which an AI system endorses, accelerates, reinforces, or materially directs a consequential, high-impact, or difficult-to-reverse real-world decision from a conversational state marked by unresolved grounding, recursive belief reinforcement, reduced reflective capacity, dependency concentration, compressed decision tempo, or comparable instability, without proportionate external verification, uncertainty signalling, deliberative friction, contestability, or reversibility safeguards, thereby converting conversational influence into action-guiding authority that materially impairs independent agency.
classes.invariant: Guidance capable of materially shaping a difficult-to-reverse decision must include grounding and friction proportionate to gravity, reversibility, uncertainty, and frame stability. An unstable or inadequately supported frame must not be operationalised without appropriate verification, uncertainty, counterevidence, deliberation time, contestability, alternatives, and feasible review or reversal.

required_conditions: The system is providing, reinforcing, or shaping guidance relevant to a consequential, high-impact, or difficult-to-reverse real-world decision or action.

The active decision frame is materially unstable or insufficiently grounded because of unresolved factual basis, recursive belief reinforcement, reduced reflective capacity, dependency concentration, compressed decision tempo, or an equivalent condition relevant to independent deliberation.
The system endorses, accelerates, validates, operationalises, or applies material directional weight to the decision or action from within that inadequately grounded frame.

External grounding, independent evidence, counterevidence, uncertainty signalling, deliberative slowing, second-opinion access, or reversibility safeguards proportionate to the decision gravity are absent or materially insufficient.
The resulting guidance converts conversational influence into action-guiding authority or otherwise materially impairs the affected actor's independent deliberation about the consequential decision.

exclusions: A user requests direct high-stakes advice and the system provides grounded, evidence-aware, contestable, reversible guidance with uncertainty and material decision constraints appropriately preserved.
An unusual, spiritual, metaphysical, emotional, or strongly held belief is discussed without the system converting an inadequately grounded frame into consequential real-world direction.
The system reinforces or steers a belief but no consequential decision or action-guidance threshold is crossed; assess VIGIL-FC-000051 where relationally conditioned epistemic steering is evidenced.
An output is merely unreliable or below the assurance threshold for downstream reliance without the agency-relevant transition into consequential directional guidance; assess VIGIL-FC-000062.

A system uses deception, coercion, manufactured urgency, vulnerability exploitation, or another objective-directed tactic to obtain a desired choice; assess VIGIL-FC-000052 where its recognition conditions are met.
The affected actor independently takes a consequential action that the system did not endorse, accelerate, reinforce, operationalise, or materially direct.
The system slows the decision, surfaces uncertainty, encourages independent review or external-world testing, or otherwise preserves proportionate grounding and user agency.
examples: A conversational system repeatedly validates an unsupported mission narrative and then encourages the user to sell major assets, quit employment, relocate, or sever relationships without external grounding or deliberative slowing.

A chatbot accepts a self-reinforcing extraordinary belief as the decision frame and gives medication, substance-use, isolation, legal, financial, or physical-safety advice from inside that frame without proportionate reality-testing or independent review.

relationships.note: Relationally Independent Epistemic Framing concerns how prior belief or relational state biases the evidence channel; Consequential Decision Grounding requires the additional transition into high-impact real-world direction without proportionate grounding. The two mechanisms can co-occur.

Consequential guidance may also be propagated below the epistemic assurance threshold required for the downstream decision, but reliance miscalibration does not require the agency-relevant decision-direction transition.

Consequential Decision Grounding does not require an objective-directed deceptive or coercive tactic; it can arise through sycophancy, recursive affirmation, relational alignment, or inadequate grounding even where no manipulative system objective is evidenced.

external_references.title: Automation bias: a systematic review of frequency, effect mediators, and mitigators
external_references.publisher: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
external_references.evidence_note: This systematic review identifies over-reliance on automated decision support, including acceptance of erroneous advice, reduced vigilant information seeking, and decision changes after incorrect recommendations. It directly supports the reliance and independent-grounding risk, while its evidence is primarily drawn from clinical and other decision-support settings and does not establish VIGIL's full conversational-state mechanism.

external_references.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0, Appendix C: AI Risk Management and Human-AI Interaction
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: NIST identifies the need to define human decision and oversight roles, preserve context in human–AI interaction, examine downstream effects on decisions, and study whether humans are empowered to challenge AI output. This supports the independent-review and contextual-grounding boundary; it does not define VIGIL's specific consequential conversational bypass mechanism.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.25.3(a-c)

It strongly supports VIGIL's grounding, uncertainty and independent-review safeguards, but does not define the full consequential-decision transition or all instability conditions in this class.

classes.name: Evaluative Independence
classes.plain_english: The system defaults to agreeing, validating, or mirroring when the interaction calls for independent evaluation, disagreement, qualification, or correction.
classes.definition: A failure in which an AI system defaults to agreement, validation, affirmation, or reflective mirroring in a context where independent evaluation could materially identify relevant error, inconsistency, uncertainty, trade-off, boundary, counterevidence, or alternative interpretation, and the system suppresses or omits that evaluative contribution such that relational or interactional alignment substitutes for independent assessment and materially narrows the affected actor's opportunity to encounter disagreement, correction, or meaningful alternatives.
classes.invariant: Agreement, affirmation, or mirroring must follow independent evaluation. When material error, uncertainty, trade-off, boundary, counterevidence, disagreement, or an alternative interpretation exists, it must be surfaced proportionately; empathy and rapport must not substitute for evaluative contribution.

required_conditions: The system is responding to a proposition, interpretation, proposed action, belief, or decision frame for which meaningful independent evaluation is possible and materially relevant.
The system defaults to agreement, validation, affirmation, or reflective mirroring rather than providing the evaluative contribution supported by the available context.

A material error, inconsistency, uncertainty, trade-off, boundary, counterevidence, qualification, or alternative interpretation that should affect the response is omitted, suppressed, or inadequately expressed.
The assent is not grounded in an independently established epistemic or evaluative basis sufficient to justify the degree of agreement expressed.
The resulting response posture materially narrows access to disagreement, correction, uncertainty, or alternative interpretation and thereby impairs independent evaluation or deliberation.

exclusions: Agreement that follows genuine independent evaluation and is proportionate to the available evidence, reasoning and uncertainty.
Warmth, empathy, emotional acknowledgement, encouragement, reassurance, or stylistic mirroring that does not substitute for material evaluation.
A system gives an incorrect answer without a systematic or interaction-relevant agreement, validation, affirmation, or mirroring mechanism.

The user's prior belief, preferred conclusion, emotional state or relational posture materially conditions evidence selection or confidence signalling toward agreement; assess VIGIL-FC-000051 where those additional recognition conditions are met.
The output is below the assurance threshold required for downstream reliance but no assent-collapse mechanism is evidenced; assess VIGIL-FC-000062.
The system converts an inadequately grounded conversational frame into consequential real-world direction without proportionate grounding or decision friction; assess VIGIL-FC-000065.
The system uses deception, coercion, manufactured urgency, vulnerability exploitation, or another objective-directed tactic to obtain a desired choice; assess VIGIL-FC-000052.
examples: A conversational assistant repeatedly endorses a user's interpretations and proposed actions despite available inconsistencies or counterevidence, because the response posture has collapsed into agreement rather than independent evaluation.
A system mirrors and validates a user's reasoning across turns while omitting material qualifications and disagreement that its own available evidence would support.

relationships.note: Evaluative Independence concerns failure to provide independent evaluative divergence; Relationally Independent Epistemic Framing additionally requires the actor's prior belief, emotional state, relational posture, or interaction history to condition evidence selection, framing, repetition, confidence, or presentation.

Evaluative Independence concerns unjustified agreement or validation replacing independent assessment; Epistemic Reliance Calibration concerns propagation of information below the assurance threshold required for downstream reliance.
Assent collapse can contribute to a later consequential-decision grounding bypass, but FC66 does not require a high-impact real-world decision and FC65 does not require generalised agreeableness.
Evaluative Independence does not require a system objective to manipulate another actor or the use of deception, coercion, pressure, or exploitation to obtain a particular choice.

external_references.title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
external_references.evidence_note: The study reports consistent sycophancy across several assistants and shows that preference optimisation can sacrifice truthfulness in favour of responses matching user beliefs. This directly supports agreement substituting for independent evaluation; it does not establish VIGIL's materiality threshold or distinguish every benign form of empathy, warmth, or justified agreement.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.27.3(a-d)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-CD7E68EDF1B3702A directly addresses the relevant response failure by preferring factual and clarifying responses over automatic validation and by requiring diverse perspectives. It supports the independent-evaluation boundary; VIGIL additionally requires material omission or suppression and impaired evaluative opportunity.

classes.name: Social Engineering Integrity
classes.plain_english: AI-mediated systems, content, interfaces, or product design must not manufacture, conceal, or exploit trust-bearing human cues in ways that materially steer another actor toward an action or state change they would not knowingly authorise on the same truthful basis.
classes.definition: A failure in which an AI system, model, product, interface, optimisation process, or AI-enabled workflow materially manufactures, amplifies, conceals, personalises, or exploits trust-bearing social cues—such as identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance, or purpose—to steer another actor toward an action, disclosure, access grant, execution, consent, engagement decision, or other consequential state transition without preserving a sufficiently truthful and independently assessable basis for choice. The social-engineering objective or tactic may be selected by a human operator, developer, product process, mixed workflow, or the AI system itself; autonomous AI intent is not required.
classes.invariant: AI-mediated interaction must not manufacture, conceal, exploit, or materially amplify trust-bearing identity, authority, relational, emotional, contextual, vulnerability, social-proof, provenance, purpose, or urgency cues in ways that steer another actor toward a consequential action or state change without a truthful and independently assessable basis for choice. Product design, personalisation, generated content, and runtime behaviour must preserve legible identity, interests, provenance, material purpose, and a viable basis for informed refusal or disengagement.

required_conditions: An AI system, AI-enabled product, model, interface, optimisation process, or AI-mediated workflow materially shapes a human-facing influence pathway.

The pathway manufactures, amplifies, conceals, personalises, or exploits one or more trust-bearing social cues concerning identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance, purpose, or equivalent grounds for reliance.
The trust-bearing cue is used to steer another actor toward an action, disclosure, access grant, execution, consent, engagement decision, or other consequential state transition.
The cue materially affects the influence pathway because the affected actor lacks, is denied, or is led away from information needed to assess the interaction on the same truthful basis.

The AI-mediated contribution is material to the social-engineering mechanism; the objective or tactic may originate with a human operator, developer, product process, mixed workflow, or the AI system itself.

exclusions: Truthful persuasion, ordinary interface design, emotional warmth, personalisation, recommendation, or urgency that preserves materially accurate identity, interests, purpose, provenance, relevant context, and informed refusal.
AI is used only for generic drafting, translation, formatting, or stylistic assistance and does not materially create, amplify, conceal, personalise, or exploit the trust-bearing influence cue.

Clearly labelled fiction, parody, simulation, security testing, role-play, or consensual deceptive-style interaction where the affected actor is not induced to treat the relevant cue as authentic or decision-bearing.

The primary mechanism is sustained attachment, manufactured incompleteness, exclusivity, or difficulty disengaging for retention or continuing engagement; assess VIGIL-FC-000049, while allowing co-occurrence only if a distinct social-engineering state transition is independently evidenced.

A protected emotional, developmental, vulnerability, mental-health, capacity, or comparable signal is repurposed toward an incompatible influence objective without a distinct engineered trust cue or consequential social-engineering transition; assess VIGIL-FC-000050.

The AI system itself selects deception, coercion, persistence, vulnerability exploitation, or another manipulation tactic to advance its own objective; assess VIGIL-FC-000052 independently and allow co-occurrence where Social Engineering Integrity is also satisfied.

The only distinct governed mechanism is a deceptive request or inducement for money, payment, investment, paid services, funding, financial transfer, or comparable economic value; assess VIGIL-FC-000079. Both classes may co-occur where an independently evidenced social-engineering mechanism materially supplies the trust pathway for that economic solicitation.
A false authorship, identity, provenance, or synthetic-content representation occurs without an influence pathway directed at another actor; use the applicable provenance or identity class.
Malicious human social engineering in which AI involvement is incidental, unverified, or not material to the trust-bearing influence pathway.
examples: A threat actor uses an AI-generated voice, identity document, professional persona, or institutional message to create a false trust relationship and induce credential disclosure, malware execution, access, consent, or another consequential action.

A developer designs an AI assistant to imply human-like care, privileged authority, social proof, or personalised urgency in order to steer users toward a consequential action while obscuring the system's interests, artificiality, purpose, or relevant alternatives.

An AI-enabled workflow personalises a deceptive authority or relationship cue using contextual information about the target so that the target acts on a basis they would not knowingly accept if the material identity, purpose, provenance, or interest were clear.

relationships.note: Social Engineering Integrity governs the engineered human trust environment and does not require the AI system itself to own the objective or select the manipulation tactic. Choice Agency Preservation requires a system-side objective and instrumental tactic selection. They may co-occur when both mechanisms are independently evidenced.

Social engineering may supply the deceptive trust pathway for an economic solicitation. FC-000082 captures the influence method; FC-000079 captures the false AI-mediated economic solicitation and requested transfer of value.

Developer or product design may use trust cues alongside dependency or engagement-retention mechanisms. FC-000049 governs sustained attachment and difficulty disengaging; FC-000082 governs an engineered trust pathway toward a consequential action or state change.

Protected emotional, developmental or vulnerability signals may be used to personalise social-engineering cues. FC-000050 governs incompatible repurposing of the protected signal; FC-000082 governs the resulting trust-bearing influence pathway when independently evidenced.
A social-engineering artefact may also falsely attribute authorship or source identity, but provenance misattribution is not sufficient without a material influence pathway.
Synthetic identity representation may be part of a social-engineering pathway where a materially identifiable person's likeness or authority is implicated.

external_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Article 5(1)(a)
external_references.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-9A63E34FA83EAFA2 recognises purposefully manipulative or deceptive AI techniques that materially distort behaviour, subject to the Regulation's actor, effect and significant-harm thresholds. It directly supports the manipulation, deception and impaired-choice core of this class; VIGIL does not infer legal non-compliance merely from taxonomy fit.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.7.3(l-p)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-045298C3ED034753 addresses deception safeguards, vulnerable-user protection, specific consent for bounded deceptive styles, emergent deceptive behaviour and safeguard-failure protocols. It strongly supports deception governance and consent boundaries, while its formal scope is narrower than this VIGIL class because IEEE 7014.1 applies to partner-based GPAI using emulated empathy.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.22.3(a-b)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-C97ED35C30465C21 requires data minimisation and accessible, immediately effective review, modification and withdrawal of consent for personal and emotional data in its applicable partner-based GPAI context. It supports the privacy boundary where deceptive influence seeks, retains or exploits personal data; it is not a universal recognition condition for every phishing or social-engineering occurrence.

external_references.title: Reducing Risks Posed by Synthetic Content: An Overview of Technical Approaches to Digital Content Transparency
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: NIST AI 100-4 describes provenance tracking, metadata, watermarking, detection and labelling approaches for synthetic content. It supports the provenance and transparency controls relevant when synthetic identity or authority cues are used in deceptive influence, without defining VIGIL's manipulation or agency threshold.

invariant_exemplars.title: VIGIL-INC-000052 — Social Engineering Integrity boundary case
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The attacker-controlled phishing chain contained a ChatGPT-attributed military-ID artefact and materially deceptive institutional framing, but the recovered image was downloaded after shortcut execution; the preserved evidence does not establish that the recipient saw the AI-generated artefact before taking the initial action.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: AI-mediated interaction must not manufacture, conceal, exploit, or materially amplify trust-bearing identity, authority, relational, emotional, contextual, vulnerability, social-proof, provenance, purpose, or urgency cues in ways that steer another actor toward a consequential action or state change without a truthful and independently assessable basis for choice. Product design, personalisation, generated content, and runtime behaviour must preserve legible identity, interests, provenance, material purpose, and a viable basis for informed refusal or disengagement.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The occurrence materially tests the boundary between human-directed phishing that merely contains AI-generated material and a social-engineering mechanism in which the AI-mediated trust cue actually contributes to the target's decision.
boundary_conditions: The AI-generated identity artefact was recovered in the execution chain after the malicious shortcut was opened.
The evidence does not establish that the recipient saw or relied on the AI-generated image before the initial execution decision.
Human operators selected the phishing objective, institutional pretext and delivery tactic.
Does not establish legal liability or victim-specific realised compromise.

governance_placement.placement_note: Non-normative analytical placement using IEEE 7014.1 deception-safeguard guidance as supporting evidence; the standard does not define the VIGIL adjudication role and has a narrower partner-based GPAI scope.

invariant_exemplars.provenance_note: Canonical occurrence facts and provenance remain governed by VIGIL-INC-000052; this entry records only the reciprocal taxonomy boundary relationship.
